story.title: Shooting at Citibank Center in Tampa Involves Employee
story.summary: A shooting incident at the Citibank Center in Tampa, Florida, involved a Citibank employee. Local authorities and company officials confirmed the incident, and new 911 calls and bodycam footage related to it have been released.

explore_lenses.label: Why does this matter for Citi’s workforce?
explore_lenses.title: A fatal attack at a major worksite
explore_lenses.summary: The shooting turned a corporate campus with thousands of workers into an emergency scene and has prompted Citi to address both employee support and site security. Authorities credit on-site security and the rapid law-enforcement response with ending the immediate threat.

claims.text: More than 3,200 people were on the Sabal Center campus when the shooting occurred; 367 Hillsborough County sheriff’s deputies responded, alongside other agencies.
Citi CEO Jane Fraser said the person killed was a colleague and said the company had counseling and other resources available for affected workers.
Forecast: Fraser said Citi would add security at its other sites as necessary while it works with law enforcement.

explore_lenses.label: How did the attack reach this point?
explore_lenses.title: Sheriff cites debt dispute and threat
explore_lenses.summary: By November 5, the sheriff had identified a reported financial-dispute motive directed at Citi rather than publicly linking the gunman to the employee who was killed. The account remains based on the sheriff’s investigation and has not been independently tested in court.

claims.text: Sheriff Chad Chronister said the alleged gunman, 35-year-old Jacob Pearson, was angry about a $2,500 debt collection and had threatened violence in a call to a Citi-affiliated attorney about three hours before the shooting.
Chronister said Pearson drove from Orlando, crashed through a fence at the Tampa campus, and shot the first employee he saw after getting out with a rifle.

The sheriff’s earlier description of the event as a targeted incident is consistent with the later account of a grievance aimed at the company, but it does not establish that the victim herself was personally targeted.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in the investigation?
explore_lenses.title: Homicide inquiry and evidence review
explore_lenses.summary: The Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office is leading a homicide investigation and has asked the public to submit relevant video. The newly released 911 audio and body-camera footage provide an early record of the response, but they do not resolve every investigative question.

claims.text: The sheriff’s office said 911 calls reporting shots fired began at 12:11 p.m.; the first marked unit arrived within one minute, and an armed Citi security guard confronted and shot the suspect in the cafeteria.
The sheriff’s office requested that anyone with video related to the incident submit it to investigators, indicating that evidence collection remains active.
ABC News reported on November 5 that new 911 calls and body-camera video had been released, expanding the public record of the response.

Because the alleged gunman died after being shot, the remaining investigative focus is likely to be reconstruction of events, motive, and any relevant warnings or security procedures rather than a criminal prosecution of him.

story_report.summary: A shooting at the Citibank Center in Tampa involved a Citi employee and left a Citi colleague dead, according to local authorities and company officials. Authorities said an armed Citi security guard confronted and shot the alleged gunman, who later died. More than 3,200 people were on the Sabal Center campus when the attack occurred, prompting a response from 367 Hillsborough County sheriff’s deputies as well as other agencies. New 911 recordings and body-camera video have since expanded the public record of the response.

sections.heading: Reported Motive and Attack Sequence
sections.body: Sheriff Chad Chronister said the alleged gunman, 35-year-old Jacob Pearson, was angry about a $2,500 debt collection and had threatened violence during a call to a Citi-affiliated attorney about three hours before the shooting. Chronister said Pearson drove from Orlando, crashed through a fence at the campus and shot the first employee he saw after exiting with a rifle. The sheriff had earlier described the event as targeted, but available reporting does not establish that the victim was personally targeted.

sections.heading: Emergency Response and Evidence Collection
sections.body: The sheriff’s office said calls reporting gunfire began at 12:11 p.m. and that the first marked unit arrived within one minute. It said the Citi security guard confronted the suspect in the cafeteria and shot him. Investigators have asked anyone with relevant video to submit it, while authorities have not released a complete case file containing all witness accounts, forensic findings or a final account of the guard’s use of force.

sections.heading: Citi Support and Security Plans
sections.body: Citi CEO Jane Fraser described the person killed as a colleague and said counseling and other resources were available to affected workers. Fraser also said the company would add security at other sites as necessary while working with law enforcement. Citi has not publicly specified what additional measures it will take or which locations could receive them.

unresolved.text: Public reporting does not establish the full history of the debt case, the contents of the reported threat call, or whether Pearson had any prior connection to the victim.

related_stories.summary: Up to 55,000 people participated in a march in Lyon as part of a nationwide strike focused on wages and purchasing power. The demonstration turned violent as police charged at protesters and deployed tear gas during clashes along the route.
